messages:
claire: heads-up: kicked off an EU backfill for telemetry v2 aggregates this morning and hit a new failure mode. about ~18 shards transitioned to STALLED with "blocked: dedupe-quota" and the requeue loop kept spinning. console showed them as 'in-progress' which confused customers. anyone seen similar? :eyes:
diego: saw the alerts. router kept routing to the dedupe hot lane even after it started returning throttle responses. we need a better short-circuit for backfills so they don't thrash the dedupe queue.
nick: logs:
```
2026-03-23T04:42:10Z WARN dedupe-queue tenant=gamma_inc action=throttle remaining_ms=120000
2026-03-23T04:42:11Z INFO router retrying request_id=rb-107 selected_lane=recompute:dedupe attempts=3
2026-03-23T04:42:13Z ERROR orchestrator shard=eu-22 id=sh-22 state=stalled reason=dedupe_quota
```
sophie: UX pain: Console labels stayed at 'running' and the customer-facing email said "job in progress". Support got tickets. We should map dedupe throttle -> explicit job state and surface a clear CTA.
claire: short term mitigation idea: add a backfill routing flag route_policy=backfill:prefer_non_dedupe=true so large backfills can opt out of the dedupe lane entirely. Ops can flip it per-run.
diego: agree. Also add an automatic demotion: if a request sees N dedupe throttles within M seconds, mark the request as 'demoted' and pick next compatible lane. That prevents infinite retry loops.
nick: implementation note: router should honor worker hints via header `x-lane-status` returned from workers. If lane reports throttle we should avoid it for backfill requests for T seconds. Cheap to add.
infra-bot: deploy: router v3.2-preview will include backfill demotion logic and `x-lane-status` handling. Canary scheduled.
sophie: for Console: mapping changes: when job is demoted show state 'waiting: lane quota' and a button "reroute to non-dedupe lane" with an estimated time/cost delta. Also show "why stalled" tooltip that surfaces last N lane responses.
claire: billing note: demoted backfills may be slower but cheaper. we should expose estimated cost delta in the reroute modal. Ops-bot, make sure billing events include the reroute decision.
ops-bot: will emit event `backfill_reroute` with fields tenant_id, request_id, from_lane, to_lane, cost_delta.
diego: also propose adding a global backfill throttle token bucket so we can limit concurrent non-dedupe backfills to avoid thrashing general capacity. e.g., global_backfill_tokens=200. when tokens exhausted, new backfills wait in queue.
nick: sounds good. We'll also attach `recompute_request_id` to every dedupe-queue call so failures are traceable end-to-end. small logging change.
sophie: UX follow-ups: (1) change console status mapping, (2) add reroute CTA + cost estimate, (3) add ticket template that support can send to customers explaining demotion reasoning. I'll PR the copy.
claire: plan: 1) ship router demotion + header handling behind feature flag, 2) update Console status mapping + modal behind flag, 3) run a canary with 10 tenants for 12h, collect metrics: demotion_count, reroute_success_rate, per-tenant latency delta, cost delta.
infra-bot: canary scheduled at 5532515600 for tenant-set "backfill-rescue-canary-10". Notifying #eng-sre and #support. :white_check_mark:
diego: add alerts: if demotion_count > 5% for backfills or reroute failures > 1% fire #pagerduty. Also log to the backfill audit stream.
nick: I'll open the router PR and add the header parsing. Claire, I'll include the `recompute_request_id` change.
sophie: I'll draft the Console modal and ticket copy now. we'll keep this behind the flag and re-evaluate after canary.
claire: thanks team. next steps documented in the RFC I'll open. tagging @diego for router, @nick for orchestrator, @sophie for Console. rolling this today. :rocket:
